newsitem.title: USA: Parretti loses latest bout in Credit Lyonnais saga.
newsitem.headline: Parretti loses latest bout in Credit Lyonnais saga.

text.p: Former owner and ousted MGM-Pathe Communications Co chief Giancarlo Parretti lost another legal battle in Delaware this week.

In an opinion released Tuesday, Chancellor William Allen of the Delaware Chancery Court refused to reopen the 1991 case in which Credit Lyonnais' Netherlands unit wrested control of the MGM movie studio from Parretti. The bank had financed Parretti's $1.3 billion buyout of MGM from Kirk Kerkorian in 1990.

In 1991, Allen ruled that Parretti breached a corporate governance agreement with the bank when he tried to have Alan Ladd Jr dismissed as MGM chief executive and when he tried to assert control over MGM's financial, legal and personnel functions.

In denying Parretti's request to reopen the case, Allen said Parretti failed to meet the legal requirements that there be new evidence that "would likely change the result reached" or proof of fraud by Credit Lyonnais.

Parretti's new evidence included a statement by his former partner Florio Fiorini that the bank had used its financial clout to pressure him to testify against Parretti. But Allen said that recantation and related documents "utterly fails to cast even a shadow of a doubt" on his 1991 ruling. Fiorini is currently in prison in Switzerland for bank fraud.

"My opinion in this case rested...on a course of conduct over an extended period of time...In the context of MGM's financial distress, Paretti's course of conduct gave the (bank) little choice but to seek to enforce their rights in MGM's stock and to oust Parretti and his allies from the board," Allen wrote.

On January 6, Parretti is scheduled to be sentenced on perjury charges stemming from the alteration of court documents in the Chancery Court case. He was convicted by a Delaware Superior Court jury in October and faces up to 10 years in prison.

In Los Angeles, Parretti's law suit seeking $3.9 billion in damages from Credit Lyonnais is set for trial in March. In that suit, Parretti has accused the bank of conspiring to "take control of MGM and Pathe from him," court papers say.
Parretti's lawyers could not be reached for comment on whether or not they plan to appeal Allen's decision.
Parretti has been free on bail since he returned to the United States from his native Italy to stand trial in Delaware on the perjury charges.
